commits.subject: Update Undertow assertions for exceptions after successful responses
Update Undertow assertions for exceptions after successful responses

diagnoses.analysis: This is the dependent aggregate gate, not an independent test failure. Its exit-1 step is selected when common or latest-dependency builds fail. All eight failed underlying jobs report the same stale Undertow post-response exception expectation, corrected by the candidate commit. No workflow change or rerun request is needed.

Both Undertow HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 tests intentionally send HTTP 200 and then throw java.lang.Exception. The PR correctly preserves status 200 while now adding error.type for that terminal exception, but the existing exact attribute assertions omitted it. The candidate expects error.type=java.lang.Exception and explicitly verifies ERROR span status, preserving all response, event and log assertions. Full default Undertow and exception-log suites pass on Java 25, as does the full instrumentation API suite. The log also contains transient Couchbase BUCKET_NOT_AVAILABLE timeouts in KV GetRequest operations. These fail before telemetry assertions, do not use the changed HTTP extractor, and are not named in the final failed-task cause; no unrelated Couchbase change is warranted.
evidence: UndertowHttp2ServerTest > test send response with exception FAILED

metadata.body:
<!--
CHANGELOG.md is generated from merged pull requests. Do not add an entry unless this PR introduces
a deprecation or breaking change.
-->

HTTP requests that fail while reading or writing the body after successful headers can report ERROR spans without `error.type`. Classify these terminal failures in the shared HTTP extractor so both spans and request-duration metrics include the error.

- **Classification:** Preserve the response status and HTTP-error-code precedence; otherwise use custom classification before falling back to the terminal exception type. Leave successful operations and existing cancellation handling unchanged.
- **Coverage:** Add shared client/server span and duration-metric regressions, plus a real Jetty HTTP 200 response truncated during body consumption.
metadata.title: Fix HTTP error.type for terminal failures after successful headers
